newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT- T-bond futures wilt in face of resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT- T-bond futures wilt in face of resistance.

text.p: Upside momentum fizzled in U.S. Treasury bond futures Wednesday as the market found itself without incentive to surpass tough technical barriers before an important economic release.

September futures were stalled near unchanged in the afternoon after inching to a three-week high of 110-05, and technicians said the contract probably would make little additional headway before Friday's May U.S. employment report.
"Any time we get above 110-02 we run out of steam," said a bond floor analyst for a U.S. trading firm.
A band of resistance punctuated by the May 13 high of 110-09, a three-month peak, was proving too daunting at this critical juncture, the analysts said.
"It should prove tough enough resistance to hold it below there at least going into the employment report," the floor analyst said.

The 110-02 level in September futures corresponds with a 6-7/8 percent yield on the 30-year cash bond, said David Eberhart, market strategist for Optima Investment Research. "That's what we're running up against," he said.
Eberhart predicted the September bond would retreat back into its trading range before Friday, slipping to around 109-16, based on waning momentum at the range highs.
For the remainder of today's session, support was likely to hold at 109-25, the floor analyst said.
Market watchers said the uninspired trade reflected a general lack of consensus about the pace of U.S. economic growth, making the May payrolls data all the more crucial.
"There is still a lot of uncertainty about where exactly this economy is heading in the second quarter, and I think a lot of people are looking forward to the report," Eberhart said.

Stewart Taylor, president of Taylor Consulting, said the fact that momemtum indicators were hitting a critical juncture right before an important fundamental event suggested market participants should proceed with caution.
"If the market is going to get into trouble at any time in the near term, right now right here is where it will do so," Taylor said.

Both weekly and daily oscillators are testing the threshold for generating buy signals, he said. "A failure of both of these oscillators to move to 'buy' will probably mean much, much lower prices," Taylor said.
